about.title: Blue Lake Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
Blue Lake is a small place. With about 1,252 residents along Davis Street, Sunrise Boulevard and the roads leading out toward Casino Way and Chartin Way, most people know each other by name, and a death touches nearly everyone in town. The public record for 2024 shows no injury collisions and no traffic deaths within city limits. Yet wrongful death claims are not limited to car crashes. A fall on someone else's property, a medical error, a defective product, or a collision on a county road just outside Blue Lake can each give rise to a civil claim under California law.

That claim belongs first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, and in some cases to other dependents or heirs. It is separate from any criminal proceeding, and it generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, sooner if a public entity is involved. LawProactive, a free service rather than a law firm, connects Humboldt County families with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Blue Lake Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can sort out who in your family holds the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock, explained
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Connecting early keeps those options open.

items.title: Every recoverable loss accounted for
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance are all recognized under California law. No fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Blue Lake recorded no traffic deaths in 2024. Can a wrongful death claim still come from something that happened here?
items.answer: Yes. Public-record collision counts only capture crashes inside city limits, and wrongful death covers far more than traffic. A death caused by a fall on private property, a medical mistake, a workplace accident or a crash on a Humboldt County road outside town can all support a civil claim. The question is whether someone else's negligence caused the death, not where the count landed for a given year.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A criminal case is brought by the district attorney and is aimed at punishment. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family to recover their own losses. The two can move forward at the same time, and the family's claim does not depend on whether criminal charges are filed or how they turn out.

items.question: What if a government agency may be responsible for my loved one's death?
items.answer: When a city, county, school district or state agency is involved, California requires a formal claim to be presented to that entity long before the standard two-year deadline, often within six months. Missing that step can end the case before it starts. Because of this, it is worth speaking with an attorney as soon as you are able.
